name: Plassey
summary: Clive’s force faced Siraj-ud-Daulah on the Bhagirathi. Mir Jafar’s wing did not fight. The nawab fled; he was killed days later. The Company had Bengal.
story: The field was wet from monsoon. The political work had been done in Murshidabad.

casualties.note: Field deaths were in the hundreds on the nawab’s side in contemporary estimates; Clive’s losses were small. No agreed integer.

reports.headline: A grove, a bribe, a province
reports.excerpt: Plassey is remembered as a battle. It was a transaction that needed a few guns to look like one.

name: Storm of Srirangapatna
summary: The Company and its allies breached the island fortress. Tipu Sultan was killed in the fighting near a gate. Mysore was placed under a restored Wodeyar with a British resident.

casualties.note: Storm deaths are described in British despatches; no single agreed civilian count.

reports.outlet: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan's Search for Legitimacy
reports.headline: The sultan in the breach
reports.excerpt: Tipu died as he had fought: in the fort, not in exile. The Company needed that death to be a victory, not a martyrdom, and never quite managed both.

name: Assaye
summary: Wellington later said Assaye was the bloodiest for its size he ever saw. A Company army beat a Maratha force trained on French lines in the Deccan.

sides.label: Maratha forces of the Daulat Rao Scindia / Bhonsle alliance

casualties.note: British returns list heavy Company casualties for the size of the force; Maratha losses are less securely counted.

reports.headline: The Deccan field
reports.excerpt: Assaye is a European-style battle on an Indian plain — artillery, infantry, a river, a butcher’s bill Wellesley never forgot.

name: Miani
summary: Napier’s force met the Talpur amirs on the Fuleli. The amirs were beaten; Hyderabad fell. Sindh was annexed.

casualties.note: Napier’s own despatches give round numbers; treat as a victor’s count.

reports.headline: Peccavi
reports.excerpt: The pun — ‘I have Sindh’ — is later folklore. The annexation was real, and the pretext remains thin in the files.

name: Ferozeshah
summary: A night battle in December 1845. The Khalsa army came close to breaking the Company line. British casualties were among the worst of the Sikh wars.

casualties.note: British returns are detailed; Khalsa losses are estimated from those returns and later Sikh histories.

reports.outlet: Amarpal Singh, The First Anglo-Sikh War
reports.headline: A night the Company nearly lost
reports.excerpt: Ferozeshah is the reminder that the Punjab was not taken cheaply.

name: Gujrat
summary: The ‘battle of the guns’ ended the Second Anglo-Sikh War. The Khalsa army was broken; the Punjab was annexed weeks later.

casualties.note: British victory despatches. Sikh combatant deaths are not independently census-counted.

reports.outlet: Khushwant Singh, A History of the Sikhs
reports.headline: The last independent army of the plains
reports.excerpt: Gujrat is where the Sikh state ends as a state. The Sikh soldier does not disappear; he is recruited.

name: Landing at Rangoon
summary: The first Anglo-Burmese War opened with a seaborne landing at Rangoon in May 1824. Disease killed more Company soldiers than the Konbaung army did.

casualties.note: Contemporary returns emphasise sickness over battle deaths. No single civilian figure for the landing.

reports.outlet: Thant Myint-U, The Making of Modern Burma
reports.headline: A war the climate fought
reports.excerpt: Rangoon was taken. The army that took it melted in the rains. Burma was not finished in 1824.

name: Thibaw deposed
summary: A short third war. British forces entered Mandalay. King Thibaw and Queen Supayalat were sent into exile in Ratnagiri. The Konbaung monarchy ended.

casualties.note: The taking of Mandalay was a collapse more than a slaughter; guerrilla resistance in Upper Burma followed.

reports.outlet: Thant Myint-U, The Making of Modern Burma
reports.headline: A palace emptied
reports.excerpt: The third war was brief. The pacification of Upper Burma was not.

name: Awadh annexed
summary: A proclamation, not a battle. The nawab was removed. Residents in Lucknow watched a court end. Sepoys from these districts would rise the next year.

reports.headline: A province taken at a desk
reports.excerpt: The annexation of Awadh is a date in a gazette. Its consequence is a year in the Doab.
